project.name: libaom / AV1 decoder
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged checkout at `_work/src/aom` on commit `5a47573f59c041e9faaf38b8e21f15affa6bcccb`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `0d6bf26dff5bacdc2455778513fb6a573eec5550`. All line anchors below use this staged tree because it matches the saved AddressSanitizer frames at `av1/common/av1_common_int.h:1236` and `av1/decoder/decodemv.c:1558`. The staged `patch.diff` and local git history correspond to fix commit `8cc8160a5cb1e2e79db9f010896d70656981f409`, which reverts the conditional `mvs` allocation.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42514031 (aom): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target av1_dec_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42514031
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `_work/src/aom` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The staged 217-byte witness with SHA-256 `93e9db35993f38c11fab2d99edeb5dc2f6bdcfe63b6c8f135a55765c6d28c102` is consumed by `av1_dec_fuzzer` as three IVF-framed payload records of 51, 51, and 47 bytes after a 32-byte prefix. Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `av1/decoder/decodemv.c:1558` in `intra_copy_frame_mvs`, and the saved allocation stack shows the overrun region was allocated earlier at `av1/common/av1_common_int.h:1236` inside `ensure_mv_buffer`. In the vulnerable code, `ensure_mv_buffer` always refreshes `buf->mi_rows` and `buf->mi_cols` and reallocates `seg_map` when frame geometry changes, but it only frees and reallocates `buf->mvs` when `cm->seq_params->order_hint_info.enable_ref_frame_mvs` is true. `buf->mvs` lives in persistent `buffer_pool->frame_bufs[]` entries, and later `decrease_ref_count()` release paths can drop a slot back to the free list without clearing that pointer. A later larger resize under `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 0` can therefore update the slot's geometry metadata while keeping the earlier smaller `mvs` allocation. When a later intra-only decode restores `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1`, `av1_read_mode_info` calls `intra_copy_frame_mvs`, which derives `frame_mvs_stride` from the larger current `cm->mi_params.mi_cols` and writes through the stale smaller `cm->cur_frame->mvs` allocation. The fix removes the conditional and always reallocates `mvs` alongside `seg_map` on null or size mismatch.

source.description: Source. Sequence-header parsing materializes attacker-controlled `enable_ref_frame_mvs` state that later controls both the stale-reallocation guard and the sink dispatch.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 217 bytes with SHA-256 `93e9db35993f38c11fab2d99edeb5dc2f6bdcfe63b6c8f135a55765c6d28c102`. `av1_dec_fuzzer` skips the 32-byte IVF header, then feeds three payload records of 51, 51, and 47 bytes to `aom_codec_decode()`. Sequence-header bits inside those payloads are read here into `enable_ref_frame_mvs`.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` only splits the witness into IVF frame records and forwards each payload to `aom_codec_decode()`. This bit read is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that turns witness bytes into sequence state used by both the stale-size mismatch and the later crash dispatch.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On a size mismatch, this guard suppresses `mvs` reallocation whenever the current sequence header disables ref-frame motion vectors, even though `buf->mi_rows` and `buf->mi_cols` have already been updated to the new geometry.
root_cause.note: The fix removes this guard and reallocates `buf->mvs` whenever it is null or the frame dimensions changed, keeping the allocation synchronized with the updated geometry.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `intra_copy_frame_mvs()` writes through a stale `MV_REF *` derived from a larger current stride, overrunning the smaller heap object allocated earlier.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at this exact line and says the faulting address is 165 bytes to the right of the 911-byte region allocated at `av1/common/av1_common_int.h:1236`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Branch-independent geometry materialization. This shared helper is the earliest staged location that the saved artifacts prove for the smaller/larger frame-geometry transitions used by the bug.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the 32-byte IVF prefix, the witness's three payload records contain the frame-header and sequence-driven state that eventually reaches this helper as `width` and `height`. Stage 01 does not preserve whether a given call's values came from `seq_params->max_frame_width/height`, `av1_read_frame_size()`, or `setup_frame_size_with_refs()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved allocation stack proves one earlier call here reached `ensure_mv_buffer()` with a smaller geometry; the crashing path later uses a larger `cm->mi_params` grid that must have been materialized here by whichever upstream frame-size arm was taken.

parser_admitted.description: A sequence-header OBU is accepted and committed here, making attacker-controlled sequence state live inside the decoder.
parser_admitted.note: Every inconsistent later sequence header also reaches this commit point and sets `pbi->sequence_header_changed` at lines 262-264. Header parsing only continues after such a change through the reset paths in `read_uncompressed_header()` (reduced-still-picture at lines 4473-4477 or keyframe at lines 4556-4561). Stage 01 does not preserve which exact payload boundaries carried those accepted toggles, so the trace models the committed sequence state and reset effect rather than naming specific frame numbers for them.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 does not preserve the exact numeric smaller and larger frame dimensions. The ASan allocation stack proves the earlier smaller `mvs` allocation came through `setup_frame_size()` -> `resize_context_buffers()`, but the saved artifacts do not establish which later frame-size arm (`setup_frame_size()`, `av1_read_frame_size()`, or `setup_frame_size_with_refs()`) produced the larger geometry used on the stale and crashing paths.

Stage 01 does not preserve which specific later changed sequence headers took the reduced-still-picture reset path versus the keyframe reset path. The trace records only the source-level fact that each accepted `enable_ref_frame_mvs` toggle that changes the sequence must pass one of those `reset_frame_buffers()` sites before decoding continues.

The concrete `frame_bufs[]` index and the exact `decrease_ref_count()` caller that made that slot free before each later `assign_cur_frame_new_fb()` are not recorded. The trace therefore grounds slot reuse in the source semantics the saved artifacts do establish: `mvs` lives only in `buffer_pool->frame_bufs[]`, `decrease_ref_count()` never frees it, `get_free_fb()` only returns slots with `ref_count == 0`, and ASan traces the crashing `cm->cur_frame->mvs` pointer back to the earlier allocation at `ensure_mv_buffer()` line 1236. `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so Stage 02 does not instrument the workspace to recover the exact slot index or final decref caller.

coarse_trace.summary: Sequence-header bytes from the witness are parsed and committed into `cm->seq_params->order_hint_info.enable_ref_frame_mvs`, and incompatible later headers set `pbi->sequence_header_changed` so decoding can continue only through the new-sequence reset path.
An earlier smaller geometry reaches `resize_context_buffers()` and `ensure_mv_buffer()`, which allocate an `mvs` array in the current `RefCntBuffer` slot reported by ASan.

Later `decrease_ref_count()` paths can drop that slot's `ref_count` to zero without freeing `mvs`, and a later `assign_cur_frame_new_fb()` / `get_free_fb()` call can rebind the freed slot as `cm->cur_frame`.

On the stale-resize decode, a changed sequence header commits `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 0`, the required new-sequence reset path runs, a larger geometry is applied to the reused slot, and `ensure_mv_buffer()` updates that slot's `mi_rows` and `mi_cols` while the vulnerable guard skips `mvs` reallocation.

Later decref and free-list reuse bring the stale slot back as the crashing `cm->cur_frame`, and another accepted sequence header restores `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1` while again passing the required new-sequence reset path.

On the crashing intra-only decode, `av1_read_mode_info()` dispatches to `intra_copy_frame_mvs()`, which uses the larger current `cm->mi_params.mi_cols` stride over the stale smaller `cm->cur_frame->mvs` allocation and writes out of bounds.

fine_trace.code:
seq_params->order_hint_info.enable_ref_frame_mvs =
    seq_params->order_hint_info.enable_order_hint ? aom_rb_read_bit(rb) : 0;
fine_trace.note: Source step. An accepted sequence-header OBU reads attacker-controlled bits into the sequence-level `enable_ref_frame_mvs` flag. The earlier `mvs` allocation in step 5 requires this parsed value to be `1`.

fine_trace.code:
*cm->seq_params = *seq_params;
pbi->sequence_header_ready = 1;
fine_trace.note: The earlier sequence header is committed to decoder state, so the upcoming allocation path sees `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1`.

On the earlier allocation path, the shared resize helper converts the current frame geometry into the smaller `cm->mi_params` grid. The saved allocation stack proves this earlier call was reached from `setup_frame_size()`; Stage 01 does not preserve the exact numeric `width` and `height`.
This earlier resize passes the currently bound `RefCntBuffer` slot as `buf` into `ensure_mv_buffer()`. That slot identity is what the later release and reuse steps carry forward.

fine_trace.code:
CHECK_MEM_ERROR(cm, buf->mvs,
                (MV_REF *)aom_calloc(((mi_params->mi_rows + 1) >> 1) *
                                         ((mi_params->mi_cols + 1) >> 1),
                                     sizeof(*buf->mvs)));
fine_trace.note: With `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1` from step 2 and the smaller grid from step 3, `ensure_mv_buffer()` allocates `((mi_rows + 1) >> 1) * ((mi_cols + 1) >> 1)` `MV_REF` elements in the `RefCntBuffer` passed at step 4. ASan's allocation stack identifies this exact line as the origin of the later-overrun heap region.

Before the later stale-resize decode can reuse the same slot, some later `decrease_ref_count()` caller must drive that slot's `ref_count` to 0. When this shared helper reaches the zero-ref block, it releases only the raw frame buffer; `buf->mvs` and the slot's geometry fields stay attached to the `RefCntBuffer`. Stage 01 does not preserve which caller performed the final decref.

A later `assign_cur_frame_new_fb()` call rebinds `cm->cur_frame` from the buffer pool's free list. Because `get_free_fb()` only selects `frame_bufs[i]` entries whose `ref_count == 0`, the new `cm->cur_frame` can alias the earlier slot from step 6 and carry its surviving `mvs` pointer into the stale-resize decode.

On that later decode, an accepted sequence header differs from the earlier one, so the decoder sets `sequence_header_changed` and commits a version of `enable_ref_frame_mvs` that is `0`. The subsequent size-mismatch path in step 13 reads this false flag.

After `sequence_header_changed`, header parsing can continue only through the new-sequence reset path. `reset_frame_buffers()` releases old `ref_frame_map[]` references via `reset_ref_frame_map(cm)` and clears order-hint state, but it does not clear any slot's `mvs`, `seg_map`, `mi_rows`, or `mi_cols`. Stage 01 does not preserve whether this call came from the reduced-still-picture branch or the keyframe branch.

On the stale-resize decode, the shared resize helper converts a later larger frame geometry into larger `cm->mi_params` values. The saved artifacts do not preserve whether these later dimensions came from `seq_params->max_frame_*`, `av1_read_frame_size()`, or `setup_frame_size_with_refs()`.

After step 10 updates `cm->mi_params`, `resize_context_buffers()` passes the currently bound reused slot from step 7 into `ensure_mv_buffer()`. This is the call whose local `buf` receives the larger geometry while still carrying the earlier `mvs` pointer.

Because the reused slot's recorded geometry no longer matches the current `cm->mi_params`, `ensure_mv_buffer()` overwrites `buf->mi_rows` and `buf->mi_cols` with the larger grid and reallocates `seg_map`. After this step, the `RefCntBuffer` metadata says 'large frame' even though its `mvs` field still points at the earlier smaller allocation.

Root-cause step. The surrounding size-mismatch condition is true, but the current sequence header from step 8 has `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 0`, so the free/allocate block at lines 1235-1239 does not run. The reused slot keeps the smaller `buf->mvs` from step 5 while its geometry fields already describe the larger frame.

Before the later crashing decode can reuse this stale slot, a later `decrease_ref_count()` path drops its `ref_count` back to 0. As in step 6, that releases only the raw frame buffer; the smaller `buf->mvs` from step 5 and larger `buf->mi_rows` and `buf->mi_cols` from step 12 remain attached to the `RefCntBuffer`. Stage 01 does not preserve which caller performed the final decref.

A later `assign_cur_frame_new_fb()` call binds `cm->cur_frame` to a free pool slot again. For the crashing path, this is the same stale `RefCntBuffer` slot from step 14, because the sink dereferences `cm->cur_frame->mvs` and ASan traces that pointer back to the earlier allocation at step 5.

On the later crashing decode, another accepted sequence header differs from the current one, sets `sequence_header_changed`, and restores `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1` in decoder state for the upcoming mode-info path.

Because the sequence header changed again, header parsing continues only through the same new-sequence reset logic. This reset still does not clear `cm->cur_frame->mvs`, `mi_rows`, or `mi_cols`, so the stale slot from step 15 survives into the later mode-info decode.

On the crashing frame, `frame_is_intra_only(cm)` is true, so `av1_read_mode_info()` takes the intra-only branch. Because the sequence-level flag from step 16 is now true, it dispatches into `intra_copy_frame_mvs()` using the stale `cm->cur_frame` slot from step 15.

The helper computes `frame_mvs_stride` from the later larger `cm->mi_params.mi_cols`, but it bases `frame_mvs` on the stale `cm->cur_frame->mvs` pointer from step 15. The nested loops therefore traverse the earlier smaller allocation with a larger logical row stride.

fine_trace.code:
mv->ref_frame = NONE_FRAME;
mv++;
fine_trace.note: Sink step. One loop iteration stores `NONE_FRAME` through `mv->ref_frame` past the heap object allocated at step 5. AddressSanitizer reports this exact 1-byte out-of-bounds write, 165 bytes to the right of the 911-byte region allocated by `ensure_mv_buffer()`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The saved allocation stack lands in the same `ensure_mv_buffer()` allocation block that the patch reworks; the stale-overflow state can exist only because the conditional at line 1234 let a later size-mismatch path keep that earlier allocation.

poc.trigger: The exact staged 217-byte witness is interpreted by `av1_dec_fuzzer` as three IVF-framed payload records of 51, 51, and 47 bytes after a 32-byte prefix. Stage 01 proved that this witness allocates one `RefCntBuffer->mvs` at `ensure_mv_buffer()` line 1236, later reaches a size-mismatch path that leaves that allocation stale under `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 0`, and finally crashes in `av1_read_mode_info()` -> `intra_copy_frame_mvs()` when a later reused `cm->cur_frame` slot is decoded intra-only with `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1`.

format.name: av1_dec_fuzzer staged three-record IVF witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 217-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `93e9db35993f38c11fab2d99edeb5dc2f6bdcfe63b6c8f135a55765c6d28c102`). After the fixed 32-byte IVF prefix, the harness reads three little-endian frame-size words `0x33`, `0x33`, and `0x2f` at offsets `0x20`, `0x5f`, and `0x9e`, then passes the resulting 51-, 51-, and 47-byte payload records to `aom_codec_decode()`. The verified trigger semantics are limited to the shared source-level states that the saved artifacts establish: the witness causes one `buffer_pool->frame_bufs[]` slot to receive an `mvs` allocation for a smaller geometry, later causes that same slot's geometry metadata to grow while `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 0` so `ensure_mv_buffer()` skips reallocating `mvs`, and later reuses the slot on an intra-only decode where `enable_ref_frame_mvs == 1`, so `intra_copy_frame_mvs()` computes its stride from the larger current `cm->mi_params.mi_cols` but writes through the stale smaller `cm->cur_frame->mvs` allocation. The saved Stage 01 artifacts do not establish which exact later `decrease_ref_count()` caller or which exact `frame_bufs[]` index produced the two required reuse points, nor which exact frame-size arm (`setup_frame_size()`, `av1_read_frame_size()`, or `setup_frame_size_with_refs()`) produced the larger geometry, so this GT does not generalize beyond this witness.
